variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, choose the color this way: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again (a color once started is finished before any other color is touched); only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start with the color of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) whose color is still needed. Do not choose the start color by required count or by a fixed color preference. Among the cubes of that color, point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color, with no distance condition of any kind; a cube is never skipped for being near the bin. If the scene at this decision step shows a detection of that color within about 10 px of that entry, point at that detection's center; if not (the arm may be covering it), point at the remembered position. The order of `cubes` is the only criterion among same-colored cubes: do not choose the cube nearest the gripper, nearest the button, nearest or farthest from the bin, or the one with the smallest y. The target is the detection of that color within about 10 px of the chosen entry in the scene at this decision step; a detection that has drifted a few pixels is still the same cube, so do not discard it, and never point at a detection lying within about 10 px of the bin center. At step #1 the first entry of `cubes` is the needed-color cube nearest the point 10 px to the larger-x side of the reported bin center, as ordered when `cubes` is filled. A point offset by a pixel or two from the detection center is acceptable; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first entry of `cubes` whose color is still needed, and if `cubes` has no such entry, choose A pointing at any visible cube of a needed color, or failing that any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), write placed=[] explicitly: the field is always output as an explicit list, even when empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. fields.name: cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each as [color, [y, x]]. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), list every visible cube of a goal color ordered by distance to the point 10 px to the larger-x side of the reported bin center ([bin_y, bin_x + 10]), nearest first (ties: smaller y); do not order by the reported bin center itself. Otherwise copy the carried-in list and: remove an entry only if the execution steps shown at THIS step include the fingers closing (about 100% to about 46% open) within about 10 px of that entry and the cube then reported 'held in the gripper'; if the shown steps begin with a cube already held, remove nothing for it. Then for every goal-color detection in the shown steps (excluding the one marked 'held in the gripper', any detection within about 10 px of the held cube's position while it is held, and any detection within about 10 px of the reported bin center), match detections to entries ONE-TO-ONE in each frame: an entry takes the nearest detection within about 10 px and only that one, keeping its slot and taking that newest position; any further detection within 10 px of that entry but with no other unmatched entry within about 10 px is a new cube and is appended at the end, in order of first appearance; a detection about 10 px or more from every carried entry is a new cube and is appended likewise. Example: carried [["red", [58, 160]]] and a frame showing red at [60, 163] and [67, 167] becomes [["red", [60, 163]], ["red", [67, 167]]]. A cube reported 20 px or more from the bin center is a real table cube and is entered even if it showed up just after a release; a cube that vanishes for a frame or two because the arm covers it keeps its entry and is not re-added. Never reorder entries, never drop-and-re-append: the list order is the age order and nothing seen later changes it. Example of a refresh: carried [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [71, 154]]] with a green reported at [68, 160] becomes [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [68, 160]]]. Cubes of colors not named in the goal are never entered. Write it as a JSON array with double-quoted color strings. e.g. [["blue", [54, 118]], ["blue", [87, 181]]]

Two things in Rule 3 have to change. First, the color-ordering clause 'take the color with the larger remaining count' is wrong and must be removed. Across all episodes with two goal colors the robot finishes one color completely before touching the other: a goal of three blue and two green was done green, green, blue, blue, blue; a goal of two red and three green was done green, green, green, red, red; a goal of two red and one green was done red, red, green. So the rule must be: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again; only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. Neither 'larger remaining count' nor 'larger total count' nor a fixed color preference explains which color is started first (the smaller-count color was started in one episode, the larger-count color in the other two), so the first color is not derivable from the goal; the instruction should say that when `placed` is empty any needed color may be started, and should name one deterministic default so the answer is at least fixed (e.g. the needed color with the larger required count, ties to the color listed first in the goal), while stressing that once a color is started it is finished before the other. Second, the clause 'simply any cube of that color' and the preference list (stable detection, not on the bin) leave the choice among several same-color cubes open, and the reports asked for a tie-break. I checked the recorded picks against the candidates: they are not the cube nearest the gripper, not the nearest to the bin, not the forward-most (largest y), not the nearest to the robot, not the first or last listed; none of these orders reproduces the recorded choices in more than a minority of steps, so the recorded cube appears to be fixed by the oracle's internal object order and not by anything the step shows. The instruction should therefore keep the hard constraints (never a cube of a non-needed color, never the bin or the button, prefer a detection present at the same place in every execution step of this decision step over one that appeared or moved mid-step) and then give one explicit deterministic tie-break so that the policy's answer is stable, stated as: among the remaining candidates of the chosen color take the one with the largest y, and on equal y the smallest x. It should also say that the point may be offset by a pixel or two from the listed detection center, which is acceptable. The fallback clauses and Rules 1 and 2 stay as they are.

When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), write placed=[] explicitly: the field is always output as an explicit list, even when empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. The literal empty list [] at step #1, written explicitly and never left blank; at every later step the field is again an explicit list. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. Count released cubes even if a cube of that color later appears somewhere on the table, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. e.g. ["green", "green"]

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, choose the color this way: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again (a color once started is finished before any other color is touched); only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start the needed color with the larger required count, ties to the color named first in the goal instruction. Among the cubes of that color, pick the oldest one on the table: point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color. If the scene at this decision step shows a detection of that color within about 10 px of that entry, point at that detection's center; if not (the arm may be covering it), point at the remembered position. Do not discard a detection for drifting by a few pixels between frames, and never point at a detection lying on top of the bin's position. At step #1 the first entry of `cubes` is the needed-color cube nearest the bin's center. A point offset by a pixel or two from the detection center is acceptable; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first entry of `cubes` whose color is still needed, and if `cubes` has no such entry, choose A pointing at any visible cube of a needed color, or failing that any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each as [color, [y, x]]. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), list every visible cube of a goal color ordered by distance to the bin's center, nearest first (ties: smaller y). Otherwise copy the carried-in list and: remove the entry nearest (within about 10 px) the place where the execution steps show the gripper closing on and lifting a cube; append, in order of first appearance, each cube of a goal color that shows up during the execution steps at a place where no entry lies within about 10 px (ignore detections at the bin's position and the 'held in the gripper' detection; a cube that vanishes for a frame or two because the arm covers it keeps its entry, do not re-add it); refresh each entry's position to the latest place it was reported. Never reorder entries: the list order is the age order and nothing seen later changes it. Cubes of colors not named in the goal are never entered. Write it as a JSON array with double-quoted color strings. e.g. [["blue", [54, 118]], ["blue", [87, 181]]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors that are on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each entry as [color, [y, x]] with the position as last seen.
